posts.content:
A lot of what we ask AI to do has three or four possible answers.

A customer helpdesk sorts tickets into billing, technical or sales, and flags them as urgent or routine. An AI agent decides whether to act or ask a human. These are small decisions made thousands of times a day, and the standard tool for them is a large language model like ChatGPT or Claude.

But an LLM is a prediction engine, built for open-ended work. It writes, reasons and explains, and it produces the answer one token at a time, running the full model for each piece. Ask it a yes or no question and you get an elaborate explanation. That is by design, and you're literally paying for all that spiel you don't even need.

Take a support inbox with 2,000 tickets every morning. Some are easy. "I was charged twice this month" is billing. "The export button crashes the app" is technical. "What does the enterprise plan cost?" is sales. For tickets like these, a paragraph of reasoning adds nothing. You want the label.

The border issues pose a bigger problem. A customer complaint that says "I upgraded to Pro and the new features still aren't in my account" could be a failed payment, which is billing, or a feature that never switched on, which is technical. A chat model replies with a sentence: "This looks primarily like a billing concern, though there's a technical element too." If you force it to return one word, the answer gets short, but the uncertainty disappears. The double charge (definite) and the upgrade ticket (possible) both come back "billing," and the output shows no difference. You are also still running a full-size model for a job with three answers.

Asking for a confidence score doesn't solve this. LLMs predict text, then get tuned on which answers human raters preferred, not on whether the answer was right.

For jobs like this, Typesafe AI built a model called Jev. Jev returns a probability for each option plus a confidence score, with no sentence around it. The upgrade ticket might come back 62% technical and 38% billing, with low confidence. The double charge comes back billing with high confidence. Typesafe trains Jev on examples where the right answer is already known, so when it says 80%, about 80% of those answers should be correct, Typesafe claims.

Confidence becomes a routing rule. High, the system acts. Medium, it confirms first. Low, a person or a larger model takes over. Because Jev writes a number instead of text, Typesafe lists output as free and input at about $42 per billion tokens. LLMs charge more for output than for input.

But two weeks after Jev launched, OpenAI announced a Decisions API for the same job. It picks from predefined answers using text or images, where Jev takes text only. Clearly there is interest in this space.

If OpenAI follows Jev's pricing logic, small decisions that never justified a full LLM become candidates for automation at a fraction of the cost. This is significant, and I'm watching out for new usecases in this space.

author.about:
When payment systems fail, someone has to figure out what's broken, what it's going to hit, what can still move, and who needs to know right now. That's my job.

As a VP at JPMorgan Chase, I run the business incident management function for global payment operations - Fedwire, CHAPS, SWIFT, CHIPS, RTP, ACH. Our function is genuinely global: based in India, my team manages Fed opening at 9pm EST and CHAPS opening at 6am UK, alongside payment operations globally - we've hit peak volumes of 13 million transactions a day. My role is command and control: assessing blast radius, determining what can execute given available workarounds and capacity constraints, driving escalation and approvals at pace, and ensuring transparent communication across operations, technology, compliance, and executive leadership - simultaneously, under pressure, with regulatory SLAs on the clock.

My other discipline is enterprise resiliency - making sure that when something goes wrong at one of our 20+ global sites, people know what to do, know they're safe, and the work still moves. That means building the plans before the crisis, running the scenarios before the event, and being the steady voice when a natural disaster, power failure, or civil disruption makes the situation genuinely uncertain, making sure people aren't stranded, work doesn't stop, and someone who knows what they're doing is already on it before the situation becomes a crisis.

Running these systems at scale for long enough, you start to develop opinions about where human judgment is irreplaceable and where the surrounding infrastructure is just slow, manual, and overdue for rethinking. That curiosity is what pulled me into AI - and I built on it outside my role, because no one was going to hand it to me. Multi-agent orchestration with CrewAI. RAG pipelines with Pinecone. Workflow automation through n8n and GitHub Actions. MCP integrations. A creator intelligence product I'm currently building. I've run models locally, tested reasoning depth across model versions, and written about what I found. I co-developed and delivered LLM training curriculum internally at JPMorgan. I did all of this while running a 24x7 follow-the-sun operations function, because the intersection of AI capability and high-stakes regulated environments is where the genuinely hard problems live - and I don't find it easy to leave hard problems alone.

I started at Goldman Sachs in 2008. Years of high-stakes operations taught me what breaks, why, and what it costs. AI is changing the answers. The problems are getting more interesting.

Interviewer/Prospective Employer:

Can you tell me a bit more about what you did at your last job?

I was Office Manager. I did all general admin, sales, tenders, correspondence, reception, customer management, BOM, Petty Cash, Personnel time keeping/leave, vehicle maintenance, travel and stay bookings (no agent). Allocate payments, release orders. Make sure Customer and Supplier info stays updated. Ensure technical drawings stay updated and properly filed. (Hard and Soft Copy) Update any changes in technical drawings with comments. (Dated /reason). And more....

Reality of 1 order: 

⚙️ Operational Flow Chart: Step-by-Step
The chart above maps out the complete sequential path of your operational workflow. Below is the quick-reference checklist for each stage:

1. Inbound Inquiry & Costing

* Log RFQ: Register customer specifications, target dates, and destination country.
* Generate Quote: Calculate material, labour, margins, and state Incoterms and currency clearly.

2. Contract & Financial Initiation

* Establish Supply Contract: Lock down terms, milestones, and penalties.
* Receive & Allocate Payment:
* Local: Match EFT to pro-forma invoice.
   * Foreign: Route to CFC account, apply spot rate, and log FX variance.

3. Demand & Production Planning

* Create Sales Order (SO): Commit the order to the master schedule.
* Explode Bill of Materials (BOM): Run stock checks on multi-level components.
* Issue Purchase Orders (POs): Order missing parts from approved vendors.

4. Workshop Execution & Prioritisation

* Create WIP for Workshop: Open the work order, issue materials, and track labour.
* Prioritise Jobs: Score and sequence active jobs using this automated matrix:
* Priority 1: Penalties imminent or critical timeline → Immediate line clearance.
   * Priority 2: Standard contract jobs → Sequenced by component arrival dates.
   * Priority 3: Internal stock or low risk → Fills capacity gaps.

5. Quality Assurance & Compliance

* Complete Test Bay Reports: Sign off quality checkpoints, log serial numbers, and attach calibration data.

6. Export Preparation & Packaging

* Prepare Documentation: Compile Commercial Invoice, Packing List, and Certificate of Origin.
* Arrange Package/Pallets: Pack to destination country rules using certified ISPM 15 heat-treated wood.

7. Logistics & Dispatch

* Local Route: Issue a Delivery Note and dispatch via local courier.
* Export Route: Hand over goods and customs paperwork to the nominated freight forwarder; collect the Bill of Lading / Air Waybill.

posts.content:
Want an opener that books meetings?

Stop switching it every week. Do this instead:

Almost every rep I speak with is stuck on the same thing:

They change their approach every week.
So they never have enough data to see if their approach actually works.

So they decide it's broken.

That's the wrong approach.
You need DATA. Not feelings.

Here's the exact process I give my reps:

1. Pick 1 opener.
Permission-based, trigger-based, or both. Honestly, any of them will work.
If you've got a real trigger, use it. If not, go permission-based.

2. Rewrite it until it sounds like you.
Not like some LinkedIn opener from a sales director who hasn't dialled in 20 years.

3. Say it out loud 10 times and record it.
Yes, it's cringe. But you'll hear every filler word and every time you rush.

4. Use it unchanged for 20 conversations.
Not 20 dials. 20 conversations where they actually heard the opener.

5. Ask your question, then shut up.
They'll usually take 3 to 5 seconds to answer. Don't fill the silence.

6. Review 1 call a day.
Did you sound calm? Was it relevant? Did you end on a question, or just trail off?

7. Only change it after conversation 20.
3 bad calls tells you nothing. Neither does 5.
You need a real sample size to know if it works.

Any opener works once it sounds natural.
And it only sounds natural after you've said it enough times.

But If you're impatient (like me), I made a tool that'll tell you exactly how to book more meetings. Not "Dial more", actual advice tailored to you.

Try it here:

https://lnkd.in/euHgxvZ4

Save this for your next call block, and repost if you know a rep who needs it.

posts.content:
GTM engineer roles are paying somewhere around $150k now. Ironic, considering a lot of the job descriptions are still hunting for the wrong person.

Don't believe me? Go read about 10 of them and come back. I bet 9 out of 10 jobs are asking for Python as a required skill. 

Most GTM engineers I know aren't writing Python. They're in Clay, HubSpot, and SQL, and a lot of them came out of sales or growth, not a CS program.

But that doesn't stop hiring managers from screening like they're filling a backend role. All because there's "engineer" in the title. 

A little "No sh*t, Sherlock" moment, but the job isn't building software. It's sales and marketing judgment.

That means targeting, intent data gathering, signal tracking, lead scoring, all handled through specific tools. 

You can teach a sharp seller enough SQL in a month. You can't teach a Python dev why a cold opener works, or how it feels to get ignored by 500 prospects and have to figure out why.

Look, I'm not saying there's NOTHING technical about the job (trust me, rude awakening). You have to be comfortable with data and wiring tools together without panicking at an API doc. But that's the floor. 

So when a company screens out an ex-SDR because they bombed a coding test, congratulations, you fired the only guy who could've helped you out of the dumpster fire.

posts.content:
Dear Distributors and Investors,

I’ve recently completed shooting my feature film, *Marriage Proposal*, in India, with a global audience in mind.

The film is an artistic, poetic, and realistic portrayal of human relationships, psychology, and emotional isolation. Having spent the past ten years studying global cinema, from its earliest beginnings with the invention of the camera, I have explored psychology, philosophy, and the art of filmmaking in depth.

At its heart, *Marriage Proposal* is a gentle, almost-silent love story that explores mental health, emotional vulnerability, and the role of women in relationships. With barely 15–20 dialogues throughout the film, the narrative unfolds primarily through the characters’ inner worlds, expressions, silences, and psychological journeys.

The story revolves around a middle-aged man who has lived in isolation for nearly half his life following a traumatic experience. When he unexpectedly receives a marriage proposal, it sets in motion a series of emotional and psychological changes as he begins to experience life and human connection in a new way.

Built around two principal characters and largely set across two locations, the film offers an intimate exploration of loneliness, healing, companionship, and the transformative power of love. The film was shot amid the beautiful hills of Dehradun, Uttarakhand, India.

I spent nearly two years developing and writing this story. I have also directed the film and acted in it. In many ways, the story resonates with my own life, making this a project close to my heart.

I am now exploring worldwide distribution opportunities and am also open to territory-wise sales. I am particularly interested in deals structured around a Minimum Guarantee (MG).

I would be happy to share the trailer and film screener upon request for your consideration.

Please let me know if this project interests you and if you would be open to discussing a potential collaboration. I would love the opportunity to bring this beautiful, intimate story to audiences around the world.

I look forward to hearing from you.

Warm regards,
Kamal Sharma
+91 99114 41012
ks@kamalsharmafilms.com

author.about:
Kamal Sharma’s interest in films began in his childhood; he’s been creative since his childhood through his paintings. After working in the corporate sector in the Human Resource Department for 13 years and leaving as the Head of HR of a group of five companies, he began his career in filmmaking. He spent long years in theatre; initially, he joined to strengthen his roots in direction, but he developed an interest in acting as well and initially started working as an actor. Later, he completed courses on Direction, Video Production, Screenwriting, Cinematography, Editing and Theatre & Camera Acting. He has spent long years studying world cinema, especially western cinema, starting from the era of silent movies and later the golden era of Hollywood from 1930 onwards. Later, he was deeply influenced by European cinema. According to him, the most crucial part of his entire study is his deep learning, understanding, and observation of world cinema. He admired the work and learned from some of the remarkable Italian, American, Indian, French, Swedish, Iranian, Japanese, and other great directors. He aims to create globally compatible projects and desires global representation. He's currently working in the capacities of director, writer and actor. Additionally, he used to study classical vocal and does so in his spare time.

Along with his continuous research and observation on human psychology, he has also studied the subject theoretically and continues to study it further to portray the best possible representation of human behavior in different situations of their lives through his characters.

A list of some directors he admires, is inspired by, and shares similar thinking, working characteristics, and interests in similar themes are: Mr. Fellini, Mr. Ingmar Bergman, Mr. Satyajit Ray, Mr. Akira Kurosawa, Mr. Andrei Tarkovsky, Mr. Kieślowski, Mr Eastwood and more, respectively.

As an actor, he has worked on feature films, short films, advertisements, television, and various theatre plays. As a director and writer, he has made short films and verticals and currently, he is working on his feature films.

One of his crime-romance-drama projects (a psychological portrayal of the journey of an orphan child coming into the crime world) and a psychological drama, romance (a portrayal of coming out of grief through love) aimed at a global audience is under production in Dehradun, and he's looking for and would like to welcome individual producers, studios, and financiers to collaborate on this exciting journey of making world-class cinema.

Cont.. In exp.

author.about:
The human brain is a crazy place, and there are two things that fascinate me most about product and growth marketing. First: the concept of consumer logic and how rational yet irrational it can be. And second: the challenge of communicating in a way that persuades and convinces consumers always requires optimization – so you’re optimizing for something that is both rational & irrational.

I apply the same thinking in product marketing & sales that I also apply in leadership, because whether you’re connecting with consumers or with your team, you’re connecting with the fun irrationality of their logic – in order to bring ideas together, influence an outcome, and also optimize and scale for future growth.

Previously, I built and led a sales team for a garment manufacturing company, bringing in 8 High profile International clients to our company doorstep, and prior to joining Trends, I worked B2B marketing across the textile and garment manufacturing Industry helping companies generate revenue.

posts.content: Breaking into pharma sales without experience is doable - and I’ll show you how, step by step. Start by learning the basics: industry terminology, common products, and the healthcare landscape. Next, build credibility-complete a short certification, shadow a rep, or volunteer in a related role. Then craft a targeted resume and cover letter that highlight transferable skills like relationship-building and problem solving. Network deliberately: reach out to current reps, attend local industry events, and join online forums-ask smart questions and offer to help. Prepare for interviews with role-play sales calls and clear stories that show impact. Finally, aim for an entry-level role or a trainee program, and treat the first year as intentional learning-track wins, seek mentors, and sharpen clinical knowledge. URGENT HIRING

JOB TITLE: ROUTE TO MARKET OFFICER

Location📍: Lagos, Nigeria
Annual Gross Salary: ₦20m - ₦30m
Industry: FMCG

About the Role:
We are seeking a highly analytical and experienced Route to Market (RTM) Officer to join our team. In this role, you will be responsible for supporting the implementation and optimization of route-to-market strategies across assigned territories and distribution channels. You will play a critical role in driving market coverage, distribution efficiency, and overall business growth.

Key Responsibilities:

· Strategy & Execution: Support the implementation and optimization of route-to-market strategies across assigned territories and distribution channels.
· Market Analysis: Monitor market coverage, product availability, distribution efficiency, and channel performance to identify gaps and improvement opportunities. Analyze route-to-market data, sales trends, and distribution reports to identify opportunities for improved coverage and channel productivity.
· Channel Management: Analyze distributor, wholesaler, retailer, and customer performance to support effective channel management and commercial decision-making.
· Field Assessments: Conduct regular market and field assessments to evaluate RTM effectiveness, customer coverage, outlet penetration, and distribution execution.
· Network Optimization: Support the development and optimization of distributor and customer networks to improve market reach and product availability. Identify new distribution opportunities, emerging channels, and customer segments that contribute to business growth.
· Cross-functional Collaboration: Work closely with Sales, Distribution, Supply Chain, and other stakeholders to address distribution gaps and improve product flow from depots to customers and trade outlets.
· Performance Monitoring: Monitor the effectiveness of existing routes, territories, and distribution models, and recommend adjustments based on market dynamics and business requirements.

Minimum Requirements:

· First Degree or its equivalent in Sales, Marketing, or other relevant discipline.
· Minimum of 5 years’ experience in the FMCG industry is required.

Required Skills:

· Strong knowledge of Route-to-Market principles, distribution models, and channel management.
· Understanding of FMCG sales and distribution operations.
· Strong analytical and data interpretation skills, with the ability to translate market and distribution data into actionable insights.
· Good knowledge of territory management, market coverage, outlet penetration, and distribution.

​🚀 Excited to share a major milestone in my MBA journey!
​I have successfully completed my internship in Retail Operations & Sales under the Store Operations vertical at V-Mart Retail Ltd.  
​During this stint, I worked on my project titled "Retail Business Operations: Fashion & FMCG at V-MART." It was an incredible hands-on experience that bridged the gap between academic theory and ground-level execution.  
​Key Learnings & Takeaways:
​Store Operations & Workflow Optimization: Analyzed daily store operations, floor workflows, and customer engagement dynamics.  
​Category Dynamics (Fashion & FMCG): Studied customer purchasing behavior to align visual merchandising and stock availability with sales goals.  
​Supply Chain Execution: Understood stock movement, inventory replenishment, and floor-level logistics to ensure smooth product availability.
​A special note of thanks to Mr. Aditya Jindal (HR) and the leadership team at V-Mart Retail Ltd. for providing me with this opportunity, along with their continuous guidance throughout this program.  
​As I complete my MBA in Marketing & Supply Chain Management at the Central University of Jammu, I am eager to apply these practical insights to full-time roles in Retail Management, FMCG Sales, and Supply Chain Operations.
​I look forward to contributing value, driving growth, and taking on new challenges in the industry!

Job Title: Field Sales Supervisors (FSSs) – Beverage Industry
Location: Lagos, Nigeria
Employment Type: Full-Time
Industry: Beverage Industry

Job Summary
We are seeking highly motivated and experienced Field Sales Supervisors (FSSs) with a strong background in the beverages industry to drive sales performance, improve market coverage, and supervise field sales activities across assigned territories in Lagos. The ideal candidate must have proven experience managing sales representatives, executing route-to-market strategies, developing distributor relationships, and achieving sales and distribution targets within a fast-paced FMCG environment.

Key Responsibilities
* Supervise and coordinate the daily activities of Sales Representatives within assigned territories.
* Drive sales volume, distribution, and market share growth for beverage products.
* Ensure effective market coverage and route plan execution.
* Monitor product availability, visibility, and merchandising standards across retail outlets.
* Support distributors in achieving sales targets and expanding customer reach.
* Track sales performance, identify gaps, and implement corrective actions.
* Conduct regular market visits to gather competitor and customer insights.
* Train, coach, and motivate field sales teams to improve productivity and performance.
* Prepare and submit accurate sales, distribution, and market intelligence reports.
* Ensure compliance with company policies and sales processes.

Requirements & Competencies
* Bachelor's Degree or HND in Marketing, Business Administration, Economics, or a related field.
* Minimum of 3-5 years' FMCG sales experience, with at least 2 years in a supervisory role within the beverages industry.
* Proven experience in field sales management, distributor operations, and territory development.
* Strong understanding of route-to-market execution and retail sales operations.
* Demonstrated ability to achieve sales and distribution targets.
* Excellent leadership, coaching, communication, and interpersonal skills.
* Strong analytical, reporting, and problem-solving abilities.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and sales reporting tools.
* Valid driver's license and willingness to travel extensively within Lagos and surrounding areas.

Compensation & Benefits
* Competitive salary package.
* Performance-based incentives and bonuses.
* Career growth and professional development opportunities.

How to Apply: Visit the weblink “https://bit.ly/3TH7op2” to apply online or send CV and cover letter to: recruitment@diversitytalent.com.ng stating the job title in the subject line

posts.content:
Ismail Industries Limited is seeking a results-oriented Area Sales Manager – Rural Business to drive sales growth, strengthen distribution networks, and expand market presence across rural territories through effective route-to-market strategies and market development.

Key Responsibilities:
- Achieve monthly, quarterly, and annual sales volume and value targets while driving primary and secondary sales growth across the assigned zone.
- Develop and execute zonal sales plans to increase market share and identify new business opportunities in untapped rural markets.
- Strengthen distribution infrastructure by developing new distributors, hub-spoke locations, and rural coverage points to expand market reach.
- Develop and implement Route-to-Market (RTM) strategies for underserved rural areas, optimizing route productivity, distribution costs, and market coverage.
- Monitor stock availability and inventory levels while ensuring efficient last-mile delivery and timely market servicing.
- Identify intelligent assortment opportunities aligned with rural consumer needs and market potential.
- Lead, coach, and monitor ASMs, TSMs, DSRs, and distributor sales teams to drive performance and ensure adherence to company SOPs and sales processes.
- Monitor claims, trade investments, and market development expenditures to ensure effective utilization and compliance.
- Prepare sales forecasts and demand projections based on business requirements.
- Present monthly business reviews and develop action plans to drive continuous improvement.

Qualifications & Skills:
- Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Business Administration
- 6–10 years of relevant FMCG sales experience, including 3–5 years in a supervisory role managing rural sales operations
- Strong understanding of distribution management, Route-to-Market (RTM), and rural channel development

Send your resume to careers@ismailindustries.com, mentioning the position title in the subject line.

Ismail Industries Limited is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives to apply.

author.description:
Ismail Industries Ltd (IIL) happens to be one of the largest manufacturers in Pakistan, founded in 1989 as a Public Limited Company.

The company initially produced high quality of sugar confectionery products under the brand name CandyLand, covering Candies, Jellies, Bubble Gums, Toffees, Chew Toffees, Lollipops, Chocolates and Marshmallows. Having one of the most advanced and sophisticated technologies in the country, Candyland continues to work on product improvement and innovation, keeping in view the changing customer tastes and demands.

In 2002, IIL launched a biscuit line under the brand name Bisconni. After just less than two years since launch, has established itself as a major player in the biscuit industry in Pakistan. IIL has further invested in manufacturing capacity to increase the production capacity as well as the capabilities to manufacture a wider variety of biscuits. 

Snack City is IIL’s latest expansion in food items. The company has invested in world’s best machinery to manufacture Real Potato Chips and other snacks.

IIL has pursued a strategy of backward integration and portfolio diversification with the establishment of Astro Pack, a unit for manufacturing of Cast Polypropylene. It is the first major venture outside the Food Industry. The CPP film produced are use in the packaging of CandyLand, Bisconni and SnackCity products and also sold to both local and international market.

IIL happens to be the largest exporter of confectionery in the country. Our products are sold in more than 40 countries inclusive of USA, Europe, Middle East and so on.

In order to maintain competitiveness in global markets, IIL has also achieved “ISO-9001” and “ISO-22000” Certification along with “SANHA” Certification considering growing Halal market in the modern world.

Job Title: Area Sales Managers (ASMs) – Beverage Industry
Location: Lagos, Nigeria
Employment Type: Full-Time
Industry: Beverage Industry

Job Summary
We are seeking an experienced and results-driven Area Sales Managers (ASMs) with a strong background in the beverages industry to drive sales growth, expand market share, and manage distributor operations within an assigned territory. The ideal candidate must have a proven track record of delivering sales targets, leading high-performing field sales teams, developing strong trade relationships, and executing effective route-to-market strategies in a fast-paced FMCG environment.

Key Responsibilities
* Achieve sales volume, revenue, and distribution targets within the assigned territory.
* Manage and develop distributor and key customer relationships to drive business growth.
* Lead, coach, and supervise Sales Representatives and other field sales personnel.
* Expand market coverage, product availability, and in-store visibility across channels.
* Monitor market trends, competitor activities, and business opportunities.
* Execute sales and trade marketing initiatives to enhance brand presence and performance.
* Prepare sales reports, analyze performance data, and implement corrective actions where necessary.
* Ensure effective receivables management and adherence to company policies.

Requirements & Competencies
* Bachelor's Degree or HND in Business Administration, Marketing, Economics, or a related discipline.
* Minimum of 5 years' experience in FMCG sales, with at least 3 years in a managerial role within the beverages industry.
* Proven experience in distributor management, route-to-market execution, and territory management.
* Demonstrated ability to achieve and exceed sales targets in competitive markets.
* Strong leadership, negotiation, communication, and relationship management skills.
* Good analytical, reporting, and problem-solving abilities.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and other sales reporting tools.
* Valid driver's license and willingness to travel extensively within the assigned territory.

How to Apply: Visit the weblink “https://bit.ly/4rXsBHV” to apply online or send CV and cover letter to: recruitment@diversitytalent.com.ng stating the job title in the subject line.

posts.content:
11 stories we are following this morning.  

1. The markets look to rebound today after a tough day yesterday.  

2. The stock of Chipotle has been rising on news of a possible takeover by Starbucks of Chipotle.  Its stock rose 6.21% yesterday.  Extraordinary CEO Brian Niccol who left Chipotle for Starbucks is the common denominator.  

3. Chipotle is down 12% YTD.  Starbucks is up 11% YTD.  

4. We did a podcast released today on “the daughter and the deductible”.   A true story of an adult child learning insurance and deductibles through work and her first full time job. A story learned at Walgreens.  Welcome to the real world.    

5.  SpaceX acquired some Spectrum assets needed for mobile phone usage and offerings.  This sent the stocks of Verizon, ATT and T-Mobile down.  The concept here  is that Starlink offers satellite coverage but offers poor coverage through walls etc etc.  This will enable SpaceX’ Starlink to better compete in the mobile market.     See “Elon Musk's SpaceX just made a huge play to challenge the phone industry and stocks like AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon are getting crushed”. Brian Sozzi Yahoo Finance.  

“Late Thursday, SpaceX said it will acquire a nationwide low-band spectrum portfolio. It positions Musk's satellite business Starlink to challenge legacy wireless giants across the US.” Brian Sozzi.  

6. The family office space is booming.  Deloitte estimates nearly 8000 family offices world wide managing $3.1 trillion through family offices.   Those family’s have a net worth in total of $5.5 trillion.  All estimated.  

7. White space and the late cancel.  I used to hate when someone cancelled a call or meeting or anything the day of or last minute.  Now I’m thrilled for it to happen and give me some open space to work on stuff.  If someone cancels on me twice, we generally make it very hard to reschedule.   

8. The outsourced CFO and finance  services market is expanding rapidly.  The market is now estimated at close to a $60 billion a year market.  

9.  I’m excited to give a keynote talk at the Business of Pain Conference today in Miami Florida.   Here we will talk about 8 to 10 trends in health care.    I’m also thrilled to speak October 20th on the evolution of AI in health care and a perspective for systems and practices advancing their use of AI.

10. The amount of foreclosed properties sold through auctions over the last year jumped.  We will see if that holds.  

11. A great pleasure this week to host our Becker's Healthcare CEO advisory call and to give a talk at McGuireWoods LLP on business development.

Mr Becker has interviewed Bill and Hilary Clinton, George and Laura Bush, Nikki Haley, Kareem Abdul Jabbar, Venus Williams and several other public figures.   
 
Scott is a graduate of Harvard Law School and the University of Illinois. At Harvard Law School he had the privilege to teach and advise future President Barack Obama as a moot court adviser.  The President was much more gifted than Mr Becker.   He hosts the highly ranked Beckers Healthcare Podcast and the highly ranked Becker Private Equity Podcast.   He is also the author of several books, a regular speaker on business and healthcare trends, a proponent of physical and mental health as a foundation to lfe and an active investor in private equity and venture capital funds and companies. posts.content: After more than 15 years working in multinational pharmaceutical and FMCG companies across sales, marketing, and training, I have learned that the strongest customer relationships are built on one essential foundation: trust. In healthcare, trust is not created by a polished presentation alone. Medical professionals expect the people representing healthcare products to understand the science behind what they discuss—and to communicate it accurately, responsibly, and respectfully. That is why I believe pharmaceutical training managers and medical representatives who work with medical professionals should have a strong medical and scientific foundation. This does not diminish the value of other backgrounds. It highlights the responsibility to keep learning and to be fully prepared for scientific conversations. My own experience with customers across Pakistan shaped this belief. During calls and presentations, I worked to be useful—not simply persuasive. Customers knew they could ask me for relevant information, discuss the latest studies, and have a meaningful conversation about the evidence behind a product.I also guided them toward practical medical resources and apps, including Epocrates and other tools they found useful. Those interactions stayed with me because they showed that respect is earned through preparation, curiosity, and consistency over time.For me, continuous learning means: Preparing beyond the product — understanding the science, the evidence, and the questions healthcare professionals may ask. Communicating with humility — answering clearly, acknowledging what I do not know, and seeking the right information when needed. Serving responsibly — remembering that every conversation about a healthcare product carries professional and ethical responsibility. When we represent healthcare products, we are also representing the standards of accuracy, integrity, and care that healthcare professionals expect. Scientific credibility is not a one-time achievement; it is built through continuous learning and demonstrated in every conversation.I remain grateful for the respect I received from customers across Pakistan, and I believe it came from being prepared to add value whenever we met. What do you believe is most important for building trust between healthcare professionals and pharmaceutical teams: scientific knowledge, communication skills, continuous learning, or a combination of all three?#PharmaceuticalSales #MedicalEducation #ScientificCredibility #ContinuousLearning #HealthcareProfessionals #PharmaMarketing

I’m an FMCG sales professional with over fifteen years’ experience in the spirits and wine industry, focused on growing brands and building genuine connections across Australia and international markets.

I was born in Łańcut, Poland — a town with a long history of spirit making — which sparked an early appreciation for history, geography and their link to wine and spirits. In my twenties, I sharpened my hospitality skills at a whisky-focused venue in Melbourne while travelling internationally as a model, experiences that gave me a global outlook and a natural ability to connect and communicate with people from all walks of life.

My career centres on commercial growth, strategic sales execution, growing a strong CRM database, and - my passion - brand development, supported by hands-on experience in events, social media, and public speaking. I’m collaborative, commercially minded, and known for turning strong relationships into sustainable results.

Whisky sits at the heart of what I do but I continue to deepen my knowledge through wine and spirit education and a genuine curiosity for maturation and ageing, driven by a love of sharing stories behind the brands and their sense of place.

posts.content:
🧳Position: Ethiopia Country Lead
🏢Company: Ubongo
📍Addis Ababa: Full-time

Requirements
 - Significant travel in-country. Need to be flexible and prepared to be ‘uncomfortable’ as some of the areas to be reached are remote with minimal amenities 
 - Bachelor Degree holder    
5 years’ related experience; e.g. education, project management, media and broadcasting, marketing and communications, business development. 
 - Technical knowledge – a fair understanding of the media and education ecosystem in the country (the Country Representative will be expected to be able to tell the team what the situation on the ground in a particular country is)  
 - Effective communication – Written and oral proficiency in English and major language(s) of the country. Good interpersonal and persuasive communication ability to be able to engage with internal and external stakeholders (role entails engaging with external stakeholders to sell the organization and content at various levels including the community level when doing eco-system interventions).
 - Initiative – self-starter, get-up-and go, knock on doors and keep on going even if doors don’t open right away.  
 - Work independently – engage with frameworks and procedures to be able to engage with stakeholders 
 - Proactive and solution oriented – very good at problem solving and decision making. There will be many circumstances that will require one to think on the spot to address issues and report back challenges faced and solutions applied (if any), to the center i.e. Ubongo afterwards 
 - Planning and organisation – there are a lot of ‘moving parts’ as the role entails working with a lot of internal and external stakeholders. Having and delivering on clear plans, coupled with clear communication, will prevent wrong assumptions and expectations 
 - Adaptability and flexibility – the role is constantly evolving
 - Have a passion for children as all Ubongo does is about the children.
 - Effective relationships and networking – the role requires the ability to build, nurture and leverage relationships is an added advantage.
Budgeting and financial reporting 
 - IT knowledge – Computer literate with basic understanding of the Google Suite and any other cloud storage software.
 - Remote working - a lot of interaction takes place over the internet (SLACK, ASANA, Google). 
 - Teamwork and collaboration – ability to work in a team environment 
Leadership – versatile leader capable of managing sideways and vertically as at the collaborative work culture at Ubongo entails dealing with almost everyone within the organization, from top to bottom.

posts.content:
My First Day at LearnVistix – A New Beginning

Today marked a very special moment in my journey — my first day at LearnVistix Pvt. Ltd., Bengaluru as a Business Development Trainee.

Walking into the office, I felt a mix of excitement, nervousness, and curiosity. As a final-year Computer Science Engineering student, starting my professional journey in the Business Development field is a new experience for me. It is different from what I have studied technically, but I see it as a great opportunity to learn skills beyond the classroom.

The office environment immediately caught my attention. The workspace was bright, modern, and filled with motivational quotes and creative decorations. The open working area, meeting spaces, comfortable seating, and the positive atmosphere made the place feel welcoming. It was interesting to see people working together, communicating, and focusing on their responsibilities.

One thing I realized on my first day is that professional life is not just about having technical knowledge. Communication, confidence, understanding people, teamwork, discipline, and the ability to take responsibility are equally important.

As a Business Development Trainee, I am looking forward to learning about sales, customer communication, lead generation, follow-ups, relationship building, and business growth. Coming from a CSE background, this experience will help me develop a combination of technical understanding and business skills.

My offer is for a three-month training period, with the possibility of a performance-based pre-placement opportunity. So, I know that these three months are more than just a training period — they are an opportunity to prove myself, learn from experienced people, and build a strong foundation for my career.

Looking back at this moment, I feel proud of how far I have come. From being a college student preparing for placements to stepping into a professional workplace, this is a milestone I will remember.

A new workplace.
A new role.
A new set of challenges.
And a new chapter in my career.

I am grateful for this opportunity and excited for everything that comes next. 🚀

#LearnVistix #FirstDayAtWork #BusinessDevelopment #CareerJourney #Freshers #ProfessionalJourney #Bengaluru #LearningAndGrowth #NewBeginnings #CSEStudent

posts.content:
We are hiring 

Project & SOW Sales – Business Development

We’re Building Something New — And We’re Hiring!

We are launching a dedicated Project Consulting & SOW Division and are looking for highly driven Business Development professionals who can think beyond traditional staffing.

This is NOT a typical IT Staffing Sales role.

We are looking for people who can penetrate client organizations, build relationships with decision-makers, identify business/technology challenges, and convert those conversations into Projects and Statements of Work (SOWs).

🎯 What will you be responsible for?

• Identify and create opportunities for project-based consulting engagements
• Build relationships with CXOs, VPs, Directors, Procurement and Technology leaders
• Understand client problems and position the right solution
• Convince clients to award projects/SOWs to us
• Own the opportunity from initial conversation through SOW closure
• Build long-term strategic relationships rather than simply chasing open requirements
• Work closely with our delivery and recruiting teams to execute the projects once the SOW is won

A smart salesperson can leverage this knowledge and network to understand:

👉 What challenges clients are facing
👉 Where we already have relevant expertise
👉 Which technologies and skill sets we can bring to the table
👉 How to create a compelling project/SOW proposal

You won’t be selling resumes.

You’ll be selling solutions, expertise and outcomes.

We are looking for hungry, entrepreneurial, consultative sales professionals who know how to get inside accounts, open doors, create opportunities and ultimately bring projects and SOWs to the organization.

💰 Compensation will not be a constraint for the right person.

If you have a proven track record of winning consulting projects, SOWs, managed services or technology engagements, we would love to hear from you.

📩 DM me directly or reach out to us to explore this opportunity.

#Hiring #BusinessDevelopment #ProjectConsulting #SOW #ConsultingSales #ITConsulting #B2BSales #TechnologySales #Staffing #USStaffing #SalesJobs #BusinessGrowth

Paycast Live Panel: How Partners Are Leveraging AI

Sell Me This Duck Signature Game
Our signature game is making its way to Puerto Rico. Stop by our setup during the event to test your sales skill, meet the team, and claim your Paycast rubber duck.

Whether you are attending in person or following our coverage online, we look forward to elevating the conversation with the fintech and sales community.

To register for IMPACT 26 or learn more about partnering with Electronic Payments, visit residuals.com.

author.about:
Alok Kumar Ghosh is a seasoned entrepreneur and financial services leader with over 20 years of diversified experience across Banking, Housing Finance, NBFCs, Commercial Vehicle Finance, Agriculture Finance, Supply Chain Finance, and Talent Acquisition. His career has been defined by building high-performing businesses, driving sustainable growth, expanding market presence, and developing strong leadership teams across India's financial services ecosystem.

Before embarking on his entrepreneurial journey, He held key leadership positions with some of India's leading financial institutions, including HDFC, Indiabulls, DCB Bank, Tata Motors Finance Ltd., Religare Finvest Ltd., and Shubham Housing Development Finance Company Ltd. These experiences enabled him to develop extensive expertise in retail lending, affordable housing finance, MSME financing, rural finance, distribution management, strategic alliances, and organizational development.
During his tenure at Shubham Housing Development Finance Company Ltd., Alok contributed to the growth and expansion of one of India's leading affordable housing finance institutions, supporting a business with an Assets Under Management (AUM) of over ₹8,000 crore, a nationwide network of 179 branches across 12 states and 149 cities. His exposure to managing large-scale operations strengthened his capabilities in business expansion, distribution strategy, operational excellence, market penetration, and customer-centric growth.
As an entrepreneur, Alok has successfully established ventures focused on Financial Services Distribution, Agri-Business, and Specialized Recruitment for the Lending Industry. His vision is to build sustainable business ecosystems that promote financial inclusion, rural development, employment generation, and long-term economic growth.

Live from Fintech Meetup Europe in Lisbon, Liam Gray sat down with Kliment Andasorov, Head of Fintech Sales, Institutional Cash & Trade Finance at Deutsche Bank, to talk about the bank’s evolving role in cross-border payments, and why the conversation is shifting from financial inclusion to financial participation.

Here’s what we covered in 10 minutes.👇

1️⃣ The bank’s role today and tomorrow
 → Where banks really sit in the digital payments ecosystem
 → What the shift from inclusion to participation means for banks

2️⃣ Banks and fintech partnerships
 → Build or buy: when banks partner with fintechs and NBFIs instead of building
 → What fintechs most often misunderstand about banks

3️⃣ Fixing cross-border
 → Where cross-border still feels slow or painful for clients
 → The technologies set to power cross-border transactions in the next few years
 → Stablecoins and tokenised deposits: threat or opportunity for banks?
 → Keeping speed, transparency and trust intact while chasing interoperability

4️⃣ Looking ahead
 → What a cross-border payment feels like five years from now

📺 Follow The Payments Shed for more conversations from Fintech Meetup Europe this week. Full episode coming soon!

#CrossBorderPayments #Banking #Fintech #Stablecoins #TokenisedDeposits #Partnerships #FintechMeetup #ThePaymentsShed

🚀 We're Hiring: Trainer – Telesales & Car Care Process | Nagpur | Multiple Positions
At Hoora, India's doorstep car and bike care network, we're scaling fast across 60 cities. Our Nagpur hub is the engine behind customer acquisition and franchise sales, and we're looking for experienced Trainers who can build a high-performing telesales team from day one.

📍 Location: Nagpur (Work from office)
👥 Openings: Multiple
🧭 Experience: 8+ years, with strong hands-on telesales training
⏱️ Joining: Immediate joiners preferred
What you'll own

🔹 End-to-end induction for new telesales hires — product, process, systems and calling floor readiness
🔹 Designing and updating training modules, call scripts, objection-handling playbooks and SOPs for our car care services and franchise offerings
🔹 Training needs analysis based on call audits, QA scores, conversion data and team lead feedback
🔹 Refresher, upskilling and remedial training for underperformers, with clear before/after metrics
🔹 Call listening, role-plays, mock calls and floor coaching alongside TLs
🔹 Certification and assessments before agents go live
🔹 Tracking training effectiveness through conversion %, talk-time, lead-to-sale ratio and early attrition
🔹 Building a TL and trainer pipeline from within the team

What we're looking for
✅ 8+ years of experience, with significant time in telesales / inside sales training
✅ Proven track record in module development and content design (PPTs, assessments, scripts, e-learning)
✅ Experience training on sales conversion, not just customer service
✅ Strong command of Hindi and English; Marathi is a plus
✅ Comfort with data: you can link training to sales outcomes
✅ Exposure to consumer services, automobile, franchise, fintech or B2C sales is a plus
✅ Train-the-Trainer certification is an advantage

Why Hoora
✨ Build the training function in a fast-scaling, founder-led business
✨ Direct visibility to leadership and real impact on revenue
✨ Freedom to design programs your way
📩 To apply: Send your CV to Amit.saxena@hoora.me with the subject line "Trainer – Nagpur", or DM me. Please mention your notice period and current location.
Know someone who fits? Tag them or share this post. 🙌 Anand Kumar Pranoti Kotangle 
#Hiring #NagpurJobs #TelesalesTrainer #SalesTraining #TrainerJobs #InsideSales #ImmediateJoiners #Hoora #CarCare #JobsInNagpur #LearningAndDevelopment

posts.content:
💡Data doesn’t tell you the truth. It tells you what you’ve measured.

Here’s a principle worth thinking about today.

We often treat data as an objective reflection of reality. But data is shaped by the questions we ask, the things we choose to measure, and the things we leave out.

A sales report might show declining revenue. But it won't necessarily tell you that customers are delaying purchases because of uncertainty, that your best salespeople are leaving, or that the market has changed.

The numbers may be accurate, yet the conclusion may be wrong.

Before asking what the data tells you, ask yourself:

What might I be missing because I am only looking at what I know how to measure?

That is where critical thinking begins. And it is where the real value of data lies, not simply in reporting what happened, but in questioning what it means.

posts.content:
Disappointing After-Sales Service from Godrej!
I am extremely disappointed with my experience with Godrej. I purchased a Godrej refrigerator just 1.5 years ago, and it has already stopped working, displaying an F1 error. What is even more frustrating is that I have been waiting for a resolution for the past 20 days! There is impossible to connect Godrej customer care. It is always very you never get connect.
Despite multiple technician visits, I have received nothing but repeated assurances that the faulty part will be replaced. The latest excuse is that the required part is unavailable at the dealership.
To make matters worse, the service team is no longer answering our calls or responding to our messages. Mrs. Nisha, who is identified as the dealership manager, has also failed to provide a concrete resolution or ensure proper communication.
Is this the standard of product quality and customer service that customers should expect from a reputed brand like Godrej?
A refrigerator is an essential household appliance, not a luxury. Keeping a customer waiting for 20 days, without a working refrigerator and without proper communication, is simply unacceptable.
This experience raises serious concerns about both product reliability and the after-sales service network. Customer trust is built not just by selling a product, but by standing behind it when something goes wrong.
I urge the Godrej management and customer support leadership to intervene immediately, arrange the required replacement part or provide an appropriate alternative, and confirm a firm resolution timeline.
I am looking for action, accountability, and a permanent solution, not another assurance that leads nowhere.
I hope Godrej takes this complaint seriously and resolves it without further delay.

#Godrej #GodrejAppliances #CustomerService #AfterSalesService #CustomerExperience #ConsumerRights #Accountability #ProductQuality

Drive the achievement of Sell Out, Reach, Range and Execution objectives for the assigned territory through the management and development of distributor sales operations and deployment of merchandising teams.

Lead the distributor sales leadership team in the creation of the annual territory business plan (ICP). Facilitate the development of operational plans to achieve reach, range and distribution objectives.
Achieve execution and quality sales standards by leading the distributor sales leadership team and consistently driving Level 2 operations review to identify specific action plans to address key gaps & opportunities. 
Drive profitable growth for distributor key customers by modelling and coaching the Nestle Way of Selling and leading excellent execution, in support of distributor customer management teams
Support the development of Category and Channel Plans by providing feedback and insight on execution and commercial issues/opportunities.
Drive the development of the distributor sales operations through training and coaching on Territory Development and In Call Execution with distributor sales team leaders.

Second always looking for ways in achieving targets efficiently ensuring low cost actions with high results. Third ensuring all companies directions swiftly implemented. Fourth ensuring sustainability of business operation in long term perspective.

In charge of the execution in all company programs and directions, in charge of the development of the area cut assigned to me in terms of volume development through improvement of sales to trade,  (UBO) or UNIQUE BUYING OUTLET meaning to ensure and monitor that all non-buying yet selling competitive products must be penetrated and eventually converted through consistent visit service by my sales personnel, right execution daily in terms of product availability, product display, SRP, merchandising and maximize utilization of other Company Assets. I am also responsible for training and development of all Distributors Sales personnel  (DSR) ensuring that they are doing their job, understands all company directions and programs, coach them in their execution in trade in terms of Merchandising, volume, UBO, call effectiveness, call compliance, asset maximization. I am also responsible for AR movements of the Distribution Partners assigned to me. Continually find ways to improve route to market execution to have an effective and efficient less cost routing system from Distributors warehouse to our outlets. I am also responsible for partner management ensures Distributors and sub distributors under me must have the complete manning and routing units for the required distribution set up.

posts.content:
It is International Mental Health Day today (on my grandparents' wedding anniversary, it would have been 86 years today, had they still been alive).

Yes, it is important to have the necessary services available and accessible to people who need them. This is the part that most people will bring up today.

The part that hardly anyone will bring up is that this is crisis and symptom management. It is also necessary, but it is not enough.

If we are serious about addressing mental health challenges and supporting people who suffer from them, we have to identify and address their root causes. 

More often than not, these root causes lie in unprocessed trauma and protective coping mechanisms that were once appropriate adaptations that were necessary for physical or psychological survival and that are no longer needed and can get in our way.

If we are serious about addressing the mental health crisis, we need trauma-proactive approaches to break down and prevent trauma walls - in individuals as well as in communities and systems. 

We need capacity building around understanding how our stress response system affects us, where protective coping mechanisms come from and what they can look like, and how we can create circumstances that allow for connection with others and to ourselves.

I am always looking for people and organisations interested in exploring how the principles of the Beyond the Trauma Wall Initiative (https://lnkd.in/g_bVmhDr) can be concretely implemented in their context or who are looking for this capacity building.

And in my new book 'The Trauma Root of Social Work: Beyond the Trauma Wall', I have outlined the underlying mechanics and dynamics and given some starting points for effecting change. You can order the book on sale here: https://lnkd.in/e3hNkMv3

Relationships, belonging, trust, and felt safety are the tools with which we can break down trauma walls in children, in adults, in families, in communities, and in systems.

#worldmentalhealthday #worldmentalhealthday2026 #internationaldayofmentalhealth #beyondthetraumawall

author.about:
I am a facilitator for breaking down and preventing trauma walls. 
To do this, I launched the Beyond the Trauma Wall Initiative (https://beyondthetraumawall.org/) in January 2025. 

Relationships, belonging, trust, and felt safety are the tools with which we can break down trauma walls in children, in adults, in families, in communities and in systems.

I aim to collaboratively find ways to address the trauma roots of many of the problems we struggle. With the goal to bring about paradigm shifts by making recognising and supporting the resolution of trauma histories a foundational part of social protection and social interaction. The initiative builds on two decades of working in child protection reform across four continents.

As an independent consultant, I connect the grassroots-level experience to policy-level guidance, providing capacity building, awareness-raising, policy recommendations, and framework development. Providing talks, briefs, workshops, and training to understand the mechanisms and consequences of trauma and how to work in a trauma-informed way, plays a big role in this. My latest book 'The Trauma Root of Social Work: Beyond the Trauma Wall' is now available to order.

What I aim to offer and achieve through collaborations and partnerships in different sectors and countries with the Beyond the Trauma Wall Initiative:
- Raising awareness about trauma walls, how it impacts individuals, systems, and societies, and how to break it down
- Training and capacity building around understanding the mechanisms behind high stress levels and trauma, what coping mechanisms can look like, what their purpose is, and what the consequences are
- Enabling a shift from symptom management and a focus on behavioural change to identifying and addressing root causes to prevent relapses and escalation of problems 
- Joint exploration of how trauma walls can be broken down in concrete ways in any sector or system by shifting from symptom and behaviour management to addressing root causes
- Raising awareness about the significant return on investment, both financially and in improved quality of life and reduction of many of the current societal challenges, of breaking down trauma walls and adopting a trauma-proactive approach. Including the potential of developing a polysolution for the current global polycrisis.

You can order my latest book 'The Trauma Root of Social Work: Beyond the Trauma Wall' (with a discount with code 26AFLY3) here: https://www.routledge.com/The-Trauma-Root-of-Social-Work-Beyond-the-Trauma-Wall/Koenderink/p/book/9781041127406

I have created the website Beyond the Trauma Wall, which has built on the trauma wall model I developed in 2024. It provides information and raises awareness on how addressing trauma as a root cause of many of the societal and personal challenges we are currently facing in the world would have far-reaching personal, social, political and even financial benefits. I am in the process of writing a book laying this out in more detail at the moment.
I am applying this as a concrete starting point in child protection reform. I am gathering a group of experts in trauma and child protection to collaborate on the development of curriculum modules for qualification training for social workers that would equip them to adopt a trauma lens in their work and address the root causes of the issues they are confronted with.

publications.title: Understanding the Trauma of Children from Institutions
publications.description: The manual was written for anyone who works on the ground to move children from institutions into families. A social worker, case manager, counsellor, or person otherwise involved in this process needs to be aware of the issues addressed in this book to make sure that the placement of children in families becomes sustainable. The aim of the training manual is to give an insight into the impact of living in an institution on children, the effects on their development and behaviour, and ways in which the families they will be placed with can handle the challenges ahead of them. This insight allows case workers to determine, through assessment, which of the issues described in the book are relevant for an individual child. It may also alert them to the need to look for specific issues when assessing the child. In turn, this helps in decisions about what kind of support the child and the family she goes to will most likely need. The manual can serve as a basis for the training – adapted to the needs of the individual child and family, and to the local context – that caseworkers will need to provide to the family to help them understand what they can expect and how they can cope with the challenges ahead.

publications.title: Understanding the Trauma of Institutionalised Children. To support the child you adopt
publications.description:
Parents adopting a child from an institution (or orphanage) are often not quite prepared for what they can expect and how to deal with it. Institutionalisation affects a child's brain development, physical development, cognitive development, emotional development and stress response. Understanding how care in an institution is different from care in a family and the effects this has on a child helps parents prepare to welcome their child and support him or her. The book also gives some advice on pitfalls and helpful approaches to caring for a previously institutionalised child, handling challenging behaviour, and helping the child catch up on delayed or skipped development. 
Areas discussed are expectation management, a general understanding of the development of the brain and the stress response system in a child, the roles of attachment, physical contact, stimulation, attention, and living in the community in child development, and the effects of institutionalisation such as attachment disorders, challenging behaviour, self-harm, and health problems. And how to help the child build trust and relationships, how to help reduce stress and establish felt safety, and deal with challenging behaviour - including positive disciplining in a way that does not cause further harm.

posts.content:
🚀 Excited to share my latest Power BI Project: Blinkit Sales Performance Dashboard! 📊
As an aspiring Data Analyst, I wanted to work on a real-world e-commerce/quick-commerce dataset. I developed this comprehensive and interactive dashboard to analyze Blinkit's sales, product categories, and outlet performance.
💡 Key Insights & Features analyzed:
• KPI Tracking: Visualized $1.20M Total Sales, 8,523 Items Sold, and an average customer rating of 3.9.
• Fat Content & Item Type Analysis: Identified that Fruits & Veggies and Snack Foods drive the maximum revenue ($0.18M each).
• Outlet Demographics: Analyzed performance across different Outlet Sizes (Medium, Small, High) and locations (Tier 1, Tier 2, Tier 3 cities), revealing that Tier 3 locations contribute the highest sales ($472.13K).
• Establishment Trends: Tracked outlet growth from 2011 to 2022, highlighting a major peak in 2018 ($205K).
🛠️ Tools & Skills Used:
• Power BI: Data Modeling, DAX Measures, and Interactive Visualizations.
• SQL & Excel: Data cleaning, sorting, and initial preprocessing.
This hands-on project helped me understand how raw business numbers can be converted into actionable, data-driven decisions for retail growth.
🎯 I am actively looking for Data Analyst Internships, Junior Data Analyst, or Entry-level Roles where I can contribute my skills in Python, SQL, and Power BI. If you have any openings or leads, please feel free to reach out or connect!

I just finished my customer behaviour data analysis project. Actually it is not completely mine, but I have written some queries and built the dashboard. 
So the workflow goes like this: I have used Python for doing exploratory data analysis, then connected that cleaned data with SQL to take out some business insights, and then finally built a dashboard using Power BI.
There are a few things I have found while doing analysis:
1. Clothing and accessories bring in about 77% of the revenue.
2. Subscriptions don't draw more revenue than the non-subscribers; both are evenly poised.
3. Young adult people have generated more revenue and sales compared to any other age category.
I am a fresher and still learning, so any feedback is welcome.

posts.content:
Signs Your Garage Door Needs Repair
October 10, 2026


Your garage door gets used every day. Changes in its sound or movement can be a sign that it needs attention. Here are five signs to watch for.

New or unusual noises

Grinding, scraping, or loud banging can point to worn or damaged parts. Have new noises checked instead of repeatedly running the door.

Jerking or uneven movement

A door that shakes, sticks, or moves crookedly needs an inspection. If it looks off track, stop using it and keep people clear.

Trouble opening or closing

If the door stops partway or reverses unexpectedly, several issues could be involved, including the opener or safety sensors. Don’t bypass the safety sensors or force the door.

Visible damage

Frayed cables, bent tracks, damaged rollers, or a visible gap in a spring are reasons to call a garage door professional. Springs and cables are under tension—leave those repairs to a trained technician.

Changes in how the opener works

If the motor runs but the door barely moves, or operation becomes unreliable, have the door and opener checked together before assuming the opener needs replacement.

posts.content:
Should private companies be able to use Nepal's national grid to sell electricity directly, and at what price?

On 1 October, the Electricity Regulatory Commission issued Nepal's first standard for calculating transmission "wheeling charges", the fee for using the national grid. For short-term open access, it set the charge at 57 paisa per unit (kWh). This opens the grid to private power traders for the first time. The Independent Power Producers' Association, Nepal (IPPAN) welcomed the move but says the rates are too high for domestic and cross-border trade.

Both sides have a serious case.

The case for higher charges: The grid was built largely with public money and loans. If private traders pay too little, the cost of maintaining and expanding it falls on Nepal Electricity Authority and, in the end, on ordinary consumers.

The case for lower charges: Open access only works if trading is viable. High fees could keep private buyers and sellers out, leaving surplus wet-season power unsold while industries still face supply gaps. Lower charges could also help Nepal export more to India and Bangladesh.

The deeper question is what the grid is for: a cost-recovery asset for the state utility, or a public platform that should grow the whole power market.

Where do you stand: protect NEA's finances, keep charges low to grow private trade, or phase rates down over time?


#EnergyPolicy #Nepal #Hydropower #PowerTrade #PolicyPulseNepal

posts.content:
What does it mean for the past to be fixed, and for the future to remain open?
Physics can orient the arrow of time. It is less often asked what gives a moment the status of a record.
In my monograph, Records, Irreversibility, and the Arrow of Time, I separate two questions that are usually treated as one:
Direction — why Entropy or complexity increases toward one side of the time axis
Status — what makes part of history fixed, while the rest remains open
The standard package answers the first through a low-entropy origin. 
The second is then treated as a corollary. I argue that this is too quick.

Within Informational Monism, temporal asymmetry is not one master fact. It is a family of related operations:
local irreversible commitment of records
complexity-resolved loss of accessibility
and a cosmic constraint against terminal saturation

A record is not merely a correlation. It is a pointer alternative anchored by dissipation. 
Once stabilized, it is undone only at an exponentially suppressed probability. 
From this, a partial order of records can be defined without requiring a global foliation of spacetime.

This monograph completes a four-part foundational sequence:
Black Hole Information — what remains available
Quantum Measurement — what becomes actual
Bell Correlations — what remains of separability
The Arrow of Time — what is fixed, and what remains open

The work does not derive the thermodynamic arrow, replace statistical mechanics, or claim a final cosmology. It offers something more limited and more precise: a clearer architecture for the difference between a world that merely evolves and a world in which something can be said to have happened.

📄 Full open-access monograph:
https://lnkd.in/dHPZGx69

posts.content:
I first used Claude in 2024 through Cline, paying for API usage. The costs added up quickly, but it was the best model I had found for thinking through plans. I’ve used it ever since. Of course, the $ 200 plan only.
Today, Claude is part of how we build Sustainity. It helps us shape ideas. We bring it a rough idea, and it challenges our assumptions, asks questions, and helps us narrow down what matters. Our product and positioning are sharper because of those conversations.
The most important role is software development. We’re building supply chain software that helps operations teams compare decisions across cost, service, risk, and carbon from choosing suppliers to planning deliveries and managing stock.
In our development workflow, Claude takes on parts of a project lead’s role, such as breaking large goals into plans, tracking what is built and what remains open, and reviewing work. One of its most useful contributions is telling us plainly when something is not finished.
We still make the final calls and verify the results. For a small team, that support helps us keep a more disciplined engineering process as the product grows.
Thank you to the Anthropic team for supporting us. We’re excited to keep building.

posts.content:
A common situation in maintenance teams: a component fails, the team pays for the repair, and weeks later someone finds out it was still under warranty.

It isn't negligence. Warranty dates sit in purchase files, contracts sit with procurement, and the maintenance team only sees the broken equipment in front of them.

In NextEAM, warranties and service contracts sit on the asset record itself. Procurement runs on a three-way match between purchase order, receipt and invoice. So when a technician opens a work order, they can see right away whether the vendor should be covering the cost.

Small details like this decide whether an asset management system pays for itself.

Does your maintenance team see warranty status when it opens a work order?

posts.content:
**RISK-WEIGHTED BACKLOG: NOT ALL WORK ORDERS ARE EQUAL**
*100 open work orders do not necessarily represent more risk than 10.*
Imagine two manufacturing plants.
🏭 **Plant A**
* 120 deferred work orders
* Most involve low-consequence defects
* Critical tasks are controlled and monitored
🏭 **Plant B**
* Only 25 deferred work orders
* Several involve critical rotating equipment
* One known defect could trigger a major production interruption
Which plant has the greater maintenance risk?
**The work-order count alone cannot tell you.**
This is why maintenance organizations should move beyond counting deferred tasks and start evaluating their associated risk.
### 1️⃣ Start with the failure mode
For each deferred work order, ask:
* What can fail?
* What is the credible failure mechanism?
* How likely is the failure under current operating conditions?
* What are the consequences?
* What controls are currently in place?
Asset criticality is useful, but it does not replace a task-specific assessment of the failure mode and its consequences.
### 2️⃣ Apply a consistent risk method
A simple screening method may use:
**Risk Score = Likelihood Rating × Consequence Rating**
Example using a hypothetical 5 × 5 matrix:
* Likelihood = 4
* Consequence = 5
* Risk score = 4 × 5 = **20**
This indicates a high-priority exposure if the site's approved matrix classifies 20 that way.
However, not every risk matrix uses simple multiplication, and equal numerical scores may represent different risk profiles. Follow your site's approved methodology.
### 3️⃣ Calculate a risk-weighted backlog indicator
One possible management indicator is:
**Risk-Weighted Backlog Index (%)**
= Current aggregate deferred-risk score ÷ Baseline aggregate deferred-risk score × 100
Example:
Baseline aggregate score = 400
Current aggregate score = 520
Index = 520 ÷ 400 × 100 = **130%**
The aggregate score is 30% higher than the baseline.
That is a reason to investigate—not proof that the plant's actual failure probability has increased by 30%.
For meaningful comparisons, use a consistent risk matrix, scoring rules, asset scope, and reporting period. Define how completed work, new deferrals, repeat deferrals, and changes in operating conditions affect the index.
### 4️⃣ Never let the total hide a critical task
An aggregate indicator can conceal a single unacceptable exposure.

#ReliabilityEngineering #MaintenanceManagement #RiskBasedMaintenance #AssetManagement #MaintenancePlanning #RiskManagement #OperationalExcellence
— Mustafa Zaki

posts.content:
Project spending to date does not tell you what finishing will cost.
A useful cost-to-complete review starts with the remaining work, then connects it to the resources and commitments required to deliver it.
Check four distinct elements:
• Actual costs already recorded.
• Costs incurred but not yet recorded.
• Open commitments for work still to be delivered.
• Remaining work without a purchase order or other commitment.
Keep incurred costs separate from future costs, and avoid counting an amount in more than one category.
Illustrative example: an open purchase order may include work already completed and accrued. Adding the full order value to the accrual would overstate the forecast.
Ask the delivery owner to validate quantities, timing and unresolved scope changes. Finance can test the calculation, but the estimate needs operational evidence.
Keep the latest estimate alongside the approved baseline, with a clear explanation of what changed.
#ProjectFinance #CostControl

author.about:
My work focuses on commercial finance, FP&A and finance transformation: connecting financial analysis with the decisions a business needs to make.
My background covers P&L management, forecasting, capital allocation, working capital and financial reporting. These areas come together when evaluating a commercial proposal, reviewing performance, planning cash requirements or improving how management receives information.
The questions that shape this work are practical. What assumptions support the plan? What changes the margin or cash requirement? Who owns the response when performance moves away from expectations?
I am also interested in making finance processes more useful through clearer reporting, better data quality and appropriate automation. A dashboard should support a decision. A forecast should explain the drivers of change. An automated process should make exceptions and responsibilities visible.
On this page, I share practical frameworks for commercial finance decisions, working capital reviews, forecasting and reporting improvement. The emphasis is on clear analysis, collaboration with the business and follow-through after a decision is made.
For recruiters and hiring leaders assessing senior finance talent, these posts provide a view of how I approach the work. Connect with me to discuss commercial finance, FP&A and finance transformation.
